service.description: Call a phone number from the current user's number fromNumber (one of their caller-ID grants; their only one when empty), through its trunk. An emergency number (VoicePolicy emergencyNumbers) is checked first and goes only through an emergency-capable trunk with the user's validated location, its callback number as caller ID and a notification destination, whatever the limits; without them it is refused (emergencyNotReady, with what is missing in the message and in missing). Otherwise the user must be allowed outbound calls, international and premium destinations must be enabled for the deployment and the user, and the limits at once and per day must allow it. Refusals carry reasonCode: notSignedIn, badNumber, notAllowed, callerIdNotAllowed, internationalNotEnabled, premiumNotEnabled, tooManyCalls, dailyLimit, noTrunk, voiceUnavailable, emergencyNotReady. The call is a CskPhone CallSession the user is in at once (callLegId) with the number ringing (phoneLegId); the same idempotencyKey answers the same call.

parameter.name: hideCallerId
parameter.description: V3: withhold the number on this call (Privacy id); empty: the user's setting (CallHandlingSetting.hideCallerId)

parameter.name: voiceTrunkId
parameter.description: The trunk it went out through

parameter.name: fromNumber
parameter.description: The caller ID it went out with (an emergency call's callback number)

service.description: Send keypad tones (RFC 4733) to the phones in a call the current user is in: digits 0-9, *, # and A-D, up to 32.
Put the phones in a call the current user is in on hold (a re-INVITE).
Take the phones in a call the current user is in off hold.
The numbers the current user may present as caller ID.

Whether phone calls can be made here (plans/Comms-Framework.md §3.1): supported (the binary has the sip feature), configured (this server's sip_port or sip_tls_port is set and a trunk is set up) and active (a SIP server is up in the cluster and a trunk has not failed), each on its own; reasonCode notBuilt, notConfigured, noTrunk, noSipServer or trunkFailed when not active. emergencyReady says whether the current user can call emergency services from here, and emergencyReasonCode and emergencyMissing what is missing (noEmergencyTrunk, noLocation, locationNotValidated, noCallbackNumber, noNotification, voiceUnavailable).
Internal (the host, while its SIP engine runs, every 20 seconds): this server's SIP engine is up, listening on sipAddress and tlsAddress with RTP on rtpPorts. stopping: it stopped; the row goes.

parameter.name: registrarEnabled
parameter.description: The edge node's registrar is on (E8)

parameter.name: edgeLinked
parameter.description: The row of this node's edge node, kept by the edge link from its Hello and liveness (plans/Edge-Node.md §5.4, E8). Never a row an engine registered, nor the reverse (refused, notAllowed).

service.description: Internal (the edge link while it is up, every minute, and the services that change a number, a greeting or a box): writes each number's PhoneNumberFallback, what the edge node's SIP engine does with its calls while this node is away: ring forwardNumber first (a ring group's outside fallback, or the user's mobile they ring with their calls and may forward to, checked against the fraud policy), then take a message (voicemailFlag, with the box's greetingLocation). Only the rows that changed are written, and a number with nothing to fall back to has none. On a paired local node, each greeting named is queued to the edge node (callAudio, keyed by its location, so each goes once). phoneNumber: only that number's.

Internal (the SIP engine of this node's edge node, E8): the bytes of a greeting or a prompt it is to play and does not have (location under dbresource://moqui/call/voicemail/greeting/ or dbresource://moqui/call/prompt/), as audioBase64; nothing for any other location or one with no file. The engine keeps a copy (their names are stamped, never written again).

On an edge node, the queue kind callAudio: a greeting or prompt of its local node (the item's content), kept at its own location (payload location, under dbresource://moqui/call/voicemail/greeting/ or dbresource://moqui/call/prompt/), which the SIP engine's fallback plays while the local node is away. Any other location is refused, and so is a local node.

Internal (the SIP engine, at start and on reload): the enabled trunks with their credentials decrypted (a trunk whose credentials do not read is logged and left out) and inboundDigest (true only for a PBX's profile: its credentials may sign a call in), the fraud policy, and the source addresses blocked now.
Internal (the SIP engine): a trunk registered, is reachable (ok), failed (errorText) or unregistered. The voice admins hear of a trunk that fails.

Internal (the SIP engine): a call came in on a trunk to toNumber. Its PhoneNumber routes it to a user, who is rung as for any call (the ring bar, Web Push), from the caller's number and name; the phone is in the call at once (callLegId, its leg). reasonCode notFound (no such number, or it routes nowhere: 404), voiceUnavailable (this node takes no phone calls: 480) or busy (the limit of calls at once: 486). Voicemail (V2): voicemail busy (the user is in a call: not rung, the engine sends it to voicemail at once) or access (the voicemail access number, PnrVoicemail); voicemailSeconds, how long it rings before voicemail. V3: a number routed to a user is handled by their rules, one routed to a ring group (PnrRingGroup) by its strategy (CallHandlingServices inbound#PhoneCall); voicemailSeconds is then how long its first step rings, and reasonCode anonymous (433) or declined (603) a refusal by the user's rules. V5: a number routed to an IVR menu (PnrIvr) or a queue (PnrQueue) is answered by the engine, which does what ivr says (IvrServices).

parameter.name: atMs
parameter.description: The time the call handling rules are read at (a spec's); now when empty

parameter.name: stepToken
parameter.description: V3: the token of the plan's first step, which the engine's ring timer carries back to begin#Voicemail

parameter.name: ivr
parameter.description: V5: a number routed to an IVR menu or a queue: the engine answers the call and does this first (as route#IvrCall's answer)

service.description: Internal (the SIP engine): what a phone leg did: answered, failed or busy (it never answered: the call ends), ended or canceled (the far end hung up), held or resumed (the far end's hold), ringing (nothing to record), or dtmf: a 1 acknowledges the recording notice when the call's recording asks for that (CallRecordingServices.ack#LegRecordingNotice), other keys are the call's own. A repeat answers as it is.

Internal (CallRecordingServices.notify#LegRecording, CallCaptionServices and Calls.js for a phone that joins later): a call's notice to an answered phone leg, played by the SIP engine of the call's node (send#SipControl, action prompt): notice recording (the recording tone), recordingAck (the recording tone twice: press 1 to acknowledge) or captions (two rising tones), each followed by the deployment's prompt audio when call_recording_prompt_audio or call_captions_prompt_audio names one. Any other leg is skipped (notified false).

Internal (the SIP engine): a failed digest attempt from sourceAddress (as username). Counted per source within the policy's window; at its limit the source is blocked for authBlockSeconds and the voice admins are told once per block. The engine counts failures itself and calls this only when it blocks a source (blocked true: block it now), so a flood from many addresses is not a database write each. It never touches a UserAccount: a scanner cannot lock a user out.
Voice status for the admin screen: the capabilities, the SIP and media nodes and the phone calls going. The VoiceAdmin permission.
The trunks, with their status and last error; never their passwords (hasPassword). The VoiceAdmin permission.

Make a trunk, or change one (voiceTrunkId). TLS with SRTP is the default; UDP or TCP signaling, or plain RTP, needs a provider profile that allows them (insecureNotAllowed otherwise). An empty password keeps the old one. algorithms: the digest algorithms the credentials answer (SHA-256, SHA-512-256, MD5), comma separated. inboundAddresses: addresses or ranges no wider than a /8 (IPv4) or a /32 (IPv6), so not 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 (badInboundAddress otherwise). The SIP engines reload. The VoiceAdmin permission.
Remove a trunk no number uses. The VoiceAdmin permission.
The numbers, with their trunk, route and emergency location. The VoiceAdmin permission.

Add or change a number (E.164 from what is given): its trunk, the user it rings, its emergency location, and its messaging bridge (C4-SMS: an SMS ChatBridge its texts go through; empty for none). The VoiceAdmin permission.
Remove a number and its caller-ID grants. The VoiceAdmin permission.
Which users may present which numbers, now. The VoiceAdmin permission.
Let a user present a number as caller ID. The VoiceAdmin permission.
Stop a user presenting a number. The VoiceAdmin permission.
The emergency locations, each with whether it is ready and what is missing. The VoiceAdmin permission.
Add or change an emergency location. Changing its address makes it not validated again. The VoiceAdmin permission.
Remove an emergency location no number or user has. The VoiceAdmin permission.
The fraud policy, with its defaults. The VoiceAdmin permission.
Change the fraud policy; what is not given stays. The SIP engines reload. The VoiceAdmin permission.

Internal: tell the SIP engine of a node (instanceId) what to do: {action: 'dial', callSessionId, callLegId, voiceTrunkId, toNumber, fromNumber, fromName, destinationClass, emergency, callbackNumber, locationReference, userId}, {action: 'answer' | 'hangup' | 'hold' | 'resume', callSessionId, callLegId}, {action: 'dtmf', callSessionId, callLegId, digits}, {action: 'prompt', callSessionId, callLegId, notice} (notify#PhoneLeg) or {action: 'reload'}. It goes to that node only, after the caller's transaction commits; a node that is gone is logged and skipped.
